Young
YUNG
adj.
Webster 1828 treats YOUNG (Yung) as adjective: not having been long born; being in the first part of life; not old; used of animals; being in the first part of growth, as a young plant; ignorant / weak, or rather having little experience. As noun: the offspring of animals, a single animal or offspring collectively. This page fills the KJV-gap adjective of the first part of life. Companion pages already treat old, child, and youth.

Biblical Definition

Young in Scripture is not a market and not an excuse. It names the first years under God, the man who must cleanse his way, and the strength that is still glory only if it is His. The psalmist will not let gray hair write a different providence: I have been young, and now am old; yet have I not seen the righteous forsaken (Psa 37:25). The BETH of Psalm 119 will not let the lad invent a path: Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word (Psa 119:9). Paul will not let the young men stay silly: Young men likewise exhort to be sober minded (Tit 2:6). John will not flatten the church into one age: I write unto you, young men, because ye have overcome the wicked one (1Jn 2:13). The proverb will not steal their strength for vanity: The glory of young men is their strength: and the beauty of old men is the gray head (Pro 20:29). The dictionary therefore keeps young from becoming either a cult or a slight. It is the Bible’s way of saying: early years — under the Word.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines YOUNG as not long born; in the first part of life or growth; of little experience. Noun: the offspring of animals, singly or together.

expand to see more

YOUNG, adjective Yung. [G., Latin]

1. Not having been long born; being in the first part of life; not old; used of animals; as a young child; a young man; a young fawn.

2. Being in the first part of growth; as a young plant; a young tree.

3. Ignorant; weak; or rather, having little experience.

YOUNG, noun The offspring of animals, either a single animal, or offspring collectively. The cow will take care of her young as will the hen. Animals make provision for their young.

Key Scripture

Psa 37:25 — "I have been young, and now am old; yet have I not seen the righteous forsaken, nor his seed begging bread."

Psa 119:9 — "Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word."

Tit 2:6 — "Young men likewise exhort to be sober minded."

1Jn 2:13 — "I write unto you, fathers, because ye have known him that is from the beginning. I write unto you, young men, because ye have overcome the wicked one. I write unto you, little children, because ye have known the Father."

Pro 20:29 — "The glory of young men is their strength: and the beauty of old men is the gray head."

Modern Corruption

Young is corrupted when youth is treated as a separate gospel, when Psalm 119’s cleansing-by-the-Word is replaced with self-expression, and when strength is baptized as a right to delay repentance.

expand to see more

The first corruption is a youth church. Psalm 37:25 is one providence from young to old. The righteous are not forsaken at either end. Segmented religion that gives the young a different Christ is not this verse.

The second corruption is Psalm 119:9 without the Word. A young man cleanses his way by taking heed to the Word, not by finding his voice. Expression is not holiness.

The third corruption is strength as delay. Proverbs 20:29 names the glory of young men as strength; Titus 2:6 tells them to be sober minded; 1 John 2:13 says they have overcome the wicked one. Strength is for war under the Word, not for a longer childhood.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Webster: first part of life; little experience; offspring. Verse-cache Strong’s on the quotations below: Hebrew na`ar (H5288) at Psalm 37:25 on young. Psalm 119:9, Titus 2:6, 1 John 2:13, and Proverbs 20:29 carry no Strong’s tag on English young in this cache; this page does not mint one.

expand to see more

Hebrew na`ar (H5288) — a youth / young man (Psa 37:25, I have been young).

Psalm 119:9 and Proverbs 20:29 are KJV-verified; the cache does not tag English young with a Hebrew number on those verse lines. No lemma is invented here.

Titus 2:6 and 1 John 2:13 are KJV-verified; no Strong’s tag on young in this cache.

Usage

"The psalmist has been young and is now old; the righteous are not forsaken (Psa 37:25)."

"A young man cleanses his way by the Word (Psa 119:9); young men are to be sober (Tit 2:6)."

"Young men overcome the wicked one (1Jn 2:13); their glory is strength (Pro 20:29)."
